gloss: deficit; in the red; red ink

definitions.explanation: A financial situation where expenses exceed income or losses exceed gains.
Text written or printed in red ink, often for corrections or emphasis.

examples.japanese: {今月|こんげつ}は{赤字|あかじ}だった。
examples.english: This month was in the red.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は３{年|ねん}{連続|れんぞく}で{赤字|あかじ}だ。
examples.english: The company has been in deficit for three consecutive years.

examples.japanese: {家計|かけい}が{赤字|あかじ}にならないように{毎月|まいつき}の{支出|ししゅつ}を{見直|みなお}している。
examples.english: I review my monthly expenses so the household budget doesn't go into the red.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}が{作文|さくぶん}に{赤字|あかじ}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: The teacher put red corrections on the essay.

examples.japanese: {原稿|げんこう}に{赤字|あかじ}がたくさん{入|はい}っていたので、{書|か}き{直|なお}すことにした。
examples.english: There were so many red corrections in the manuscript that I decided to rewrite it.

notes:
{赤字|あかじ} literally means 'red letters', from the practice of recording losses in red ink.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {赤字|あかじ}になる (to go into the red)
- {赤字|あかじ}を{出|だ}す (to incur a loss)
- {赤字|あかじ}{経営|けいえい} (operating at a loss)
- {赤字|あかじ}{国債|こくさい} (deficit-covering bonds)
- {財政|ざいせい}{赤字|あかじ} (fiscal deficit)

CONTRAST:
- {赤字|あかじ} (deficit, in the red)
- {黒字|くろじ} (surplus, in the black)

NOTE:
In Japanese accounting, losses traditionally were written in red ({赤|あか}), while profits were in black ({黒|くろ}), similar to Western conventions.
